config.title: Routing

intro.title: Routing
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple web server using Express that responds to different URL paths, like '/home' and '/about', with custom messages. You'll learn the core concept of routing, which directs incoming HTTP requests to the appropriate handler functions based on the request's URL and method. The main technologies involved are the Express framework and its built-in routing methods, such as app.get() and app.post(). By the end, you'll understand how to define routes and send responses, forming the foundation for building more complex web applications.
intro.usecase: Routing is fundamental to every web application built with Express, determining how the server responds to client requests for different URLs. In e-commerce sites, routing handles product pages, shopping carts, and checkout processes—each with its own endpoint. Content management systems use routing to serve articles, user profiles, and admin panels from distinct paths. As a developer, you'll implement routing to organize your application's structure, manage user navigation, and ensure the right content loads for each page request.

objectives: Implement basic route handlers for HTTP GET requests in Express
Configure route parameters to capture dynamic values from URLs
Construct route handlers that respond with appropriate HTTP status codes
Apply route chaining to handle multiple HTTP methods on the same path
Initialize and use Express Router to organize routes into modular units
Manipulate request and response objects within route handlers to process and return data
Integrate middleware functions into specific routes for request processing

steps.title: Import Express framework
steps.instruction: Import the Express module using require() to make Express functionality available in your application.
steps.hint: Use the require() function to import the 'express' module and assign it to a variable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a module in Node.js
const fs = require('fs');
steps.expectedOutcome: Express is imported and ready to be used to create a web server.
successCriteria: The Express module is imported using require() and assigned to a variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using require() to import the 'express' module and assigning it to a variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: import the Express module using require() so you can use it to create a web server.

steps.title: Create Express application instance
steps.instruction: Create an Express application instance by calling the Express function and assigning it to a variable named 'app'.
steps.hint: Call the imported Express function (without 'new') and store the result in a variable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating an application instance
const app = express();
steps.seedCode:
const express = require('express');

// Create your Express app instance here
steps.expectedOutcome: The Express application instance is created and ready to handle routes.
successCriteria: Variable 'app' is declared and assigned the result of calling express().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling express() and assigning it to a variable named 'app'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Express application instance wasn't created correctly. Review how to initialize an Express app.

steps.title: Define a GET route for the root path
steps.instruction: Use the app.get() method to define a route handler that responds to GET requests at the root path ('/') with a simple text response.
steps.hint: Call app.get() with two arguments: the path string '/' and a callback function that takes request and response parameters. Inside the callback, use res.send() to send a response.
steps.expectedOutcome: The app will have a route handler that responds to GET requests at '/' with a text response.
successCriteria: The app.get() method is called with '/' as the first argument and a callback function that uses res.send() to send a response.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're calling app.get() with the path '/' and a callback function that uses res.send().
steps.feedbackWrong: The route handler isn't defined correctly. Remember to use app.get('/', callback) where the callback sends a response with res.send().

steps.title: Define a GET route for '/about' path
steps.instruction: Add another app.get() route handler for the '/about' path that sends a different response text.
steps.hint: Use the same pattern as the root route, but change the path to '/about' and the response text to something like 'About page'.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your Express app will now respond to GET requests at both '/' and '/about' with different messages.
successCriteria: A new app.get() route is defined for the '/about' path that sends a response.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using app.get() with '/about' and sending a response.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added a new app.get() route for '/about' that sends a response.

steps.title: Define a POST route for '/submit' path
steps.instruction: Add a POST route for the '/submit' path that sends a response acknowledging a form submission.
steps.hint: Use app.post() with the path '/submit' and a callback function that takes req and res parameters. Inside the callback, use res.send() to send a response message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will now handle POST requests to '/submit' and respond with an acknowledgment message.
successCriteria: A POST route for '/submit' is defined using app.post() and sends a response with a message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a route, but it might not be a POST route or the path might be incorrect. Check that you used app.post() with '/submit' and included a response.
steps.feedbackWrong: The POST route for '/submit' is not correctly defined. Ensure you use app.post() with the correct path and send a response.

steps.title: Define a route with URL parameters
steps.instruction: Define a GET route for '/users/:id' that captures the id parameter and sends a response like 'User ID: [id]'.
steps.hint: Use app.get() with '/users/:id' as the path. The parameter value will be available in req.params.id.
steps.expectedOutcome: A dynamic route that captures user IDs from the URL and responds with the captured ID.
successCriteria: A GET route for '/users/:id' is defined that uses req.params.id in the response.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your route path includes ':id' and you're using req.params.id in the response.
steps.feedbackWrong: The route wasn't defined correctly. Check that you used app.get() with '/users/:id' and accessed the parameter value.

steps.title: Define a route with multiple URL parameters
steps.instruction: Define a GET route for '/books/:category/:id' that captures both URL parameters and sends a response using them.
steps.hint: Use app.get() with the path containing two colon-prefixed parameters, then access them via req.params in the handler.
steps.expectedOutcome: A route that responds to GET requests at '/books/:category/:id' and uses both captured parameters in the response.
successCriteria: The route is defined with app.get('/books/:category/:id', handler), and the handler sends a response containing both req.params.category and req.params.id.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your route path includes both :category and :id parameters, and that you're using req.params to access them in the response.
steps.feedbackWrong: The route definition is incomplete or incorrect. Remember to use app.get() with '/books/:category/:id' and access both parameters via req.params in the handler function.

steps.title: Define a route with query parameters
steps.instruction: Define a GET route for '/search' that accesses query parameters from req.query and uses them in the response.
steps.hint: Use app.get() with '/search' as the path. In the handler function, access query parameters like req.query.q and send a response that includes them.
steps.expectedOutcome: A GET route for '/search' that reads query parameters (e.g., req.query.q) and sends a response containing them.
successCriteria: The route is defined with app.get('/search', handler). The handler accesses req.query and uses at least one query parameter in the response.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your route handler accesses req.query and uses a query parameter in the response message.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you defined a GET route for '/search' and used req.query to access query parameters in the response.

steps.title: Start the server to listen on a port
steps.instruction: Add the app.listen() method to start your Express server on port 3000 and log a startup message to the console.
steps.hint: Call app.listen() with port 3000 and a callback function that logs a message like 'Server is running on port 3000'.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your Express server will be configured to listen on port 3000 and log a startup message when it begins running.
successCriteria: The app.listen() method is called with port 3000 and a callback function that logs a startup message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're calling app.listen() with both the port number (3000) and a callback function that logs a message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't started yet. You need to call app.listen() with port 3000 and a callback function to log a startup message.

steps.title: Test all routes with the running server
steps.instruction: Run your Express application and test each route (root, about, submit, parameter routes) to ensure they respond correctly.
steps.hint: Use node to run your file, then open a browser or use a tool like curl or Postman to send requests to your routes.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your server will run and respond correctly to requests for all defined routes.
successCriteria: The application runs without errors, and each route responds with the expected message when tested.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Your server runs, but some routes might not be responding as expected. Check that all route definitions are complete and correctly placed.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't running or routes aren't responding. Make sure you've defined all routes and started the server with app.listen().
